scope: CBSE Class 6 Mathematics · Ganita Prakash · Chapter 3 · Number Play
claimBoundary: This is deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios. It is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, accessibility certification, or school-specific pacing validation.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 3 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked required assessment type, a privacy-safe learner action, and an observable mastery criterion. Number-process and conjecture activities must distinguish evidence from proof, and all learner work must remain possible without camera, microphone, cloud AI, precise location, remote monitoring, or live-school data collection.

scenarios.need: Learner compares large numbers by how the digit strings look rather than by the highest place at which the numbers differ.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: comparing numbers from visual digit appearance rather than place value
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Write the two numbers in aligned place-value columns, mark the first position where they differ, and justify the comparison from that place without uploading the work.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly compares three new five- or six-digit pairs and explains each decision from the highest differing place value rather than visual appearance.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes equally spaced number-line marks always increase by one and ignores the values of the labelled anchors.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: assuming every equally spaced number-line mark increases by one
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Subtract two labelled anchor values, count the equal numerical intervals between them, divide to find the interval value, and place new values on a hand-drawn line.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Derives the correct interval value and places at least three new values correctly on a different equally spaced number line while explaining why physical spacing alone does not set the numerical interval.

scenarios.need: Learner thinks the digit sum identifies a unique number and therefore expects different numbers to have different digit sums.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: digit sum uniquely identifies a number
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compute digit sums for several rearrangements of the same digits on paper, then compare the resulting numbers and digit sums as separate properties.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Produces two different numbers with the same digit sum, calculates both sums correctly, and explains why place value can change while the digit sum stays unchanged.

scenarios.need: Learner treats a leading zero created by digit reversal as a new place-value position and records an incorrect numerical value.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: leading zeroes create new place value after reversal
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Reverse several three-digit numerals including one ending in zero, write both the reversed digit string and its numerical value, and explain the role of a leading zero.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly handles at least three reversal cases including an ending-zero case and states that a leading zero does not create extra numerical place value.

scenarios.need: Learner generalises from many successful trials of a number process and calls the resulting universal statement proved.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: many successful examples prove a rule for every starting number
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Run a fixed number process on a small paper table of examples, record the observations, and label any unsupported universal statement as an observation or conjecture rather than a theorem.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Given a fresh finite-testing example, distinguishes observed evidence from universal proof and uses the terms observation, conjecture and proven fact appropriately.

scenarios.need: Learner rejects a useful estimate because it does not equal the exact answer.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: an estimate must equal the exact answer
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Round two calculation problems to friendly values, record an estimate, then calculate exactly and compare the two results as a reasonableness check.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Produces reasonable estimates for three new calculations, obtains the exact answers separately, and explains why a useful estimate may differ from the exact value.

scenarios.need: Learner finds a successful move once in a number game and describes that single outcome as a winning strategy without a repeatable rule.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: one successful move is a winning strategy
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Describe the rule that would be repeated on later turns, test it on several synthetic game states, and separate a repeatable strategy from a lucky one-off result.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains a repeatable rule for a fresh synthetic number-game situation and correctly distinguishes strategy evidence from one isolated successful move.

scenarios.need: Learner needs a fully offline route for Number Play and cannot depend on video, microphone, camera, cloud AI, precise location, telemetry, or remote teacher monitoring.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached Kiki text, locally rendered number examples, paper and pencil, and locally available assessment interactions; no network-dependent tutoring step or media capture is required.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes a mental-method example, an estimation check and the mastery task using only offline local resources, with correct reasoning and no network-dependent tutoring step.
